basis: Severe brain, limb and airway malformations define the syndrome; cardiac malformations occur in 30-79%. Oral clefts (30-79%) omitted at the four-axis cap.
Intrinsic skeletal muscle disease with nemaline bodies and weakness; respiratory and swallowing dysfunction arise from muscle weakness, without established lung or gut damage.
Synostoses, eyelid defects and learning disability characterize the syndrome; hearing impairment occurs in 80-99%. Oral clefts (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Viral infection with hepatocellular injury (80-99%); renal injury and abnormal bleeding are annotated at 30-79%. Shock and encephalopathy are minority complications.
Tumor arises in endocrine pancreatic beta cells. Neuroglycopenic episodes do not establish lasting neurologic damage; associated MEN1 tumors are separate diseases.
Intellectual disability, microcephaly and joint contractures define the syndrome. Frequencies and functional significance of additional skin and eyelid findings are unclear.
Immune-mediated rheumatic disease of a cardiac valve; the pulmonary valve belongs to the cardiovascular axis.
A neurologic movement disorder affecting orofacial movements; the location of abnormal movements does not establish intrinsic oral tissue damage.
Generalized epilepsy with developmental impairment and cognitive regression; no other organ has qualifying common damage.
The defining features are eyelid ptosis, skeletal syndactyly and neurodevelopmental learning difficulties.
Skeletal dysplasia, palatal defects and ptosis define the syndrome. Hydronephrosis occurs in 3/4 patients; cardiac anomalies lack a clear frequency and are omitted at cap.
Woolly sparse hair defines the disorder. Protruding ears and an everted lip do not establish hearing impairment or intrinsic gastrointestinal damage.
Interferonopathy with defining aortic calcification and skeletal disease; dental dysplasia is a defining diagnostic feature. Psoriasiform skin disease omitted at cap.
Congenital contractures and arthrogryposis occur in 3/3. An absent fetal stomach bubble does not establish intrinsic gastrointestinal damage; no neural lesion is documented.
Complement deficiency is an immunodeficiency. Recurrent meningococcal infection is a separately diagnosed infection, not evidence of intrinsic neurologic involvement.
The supplied name defines cleft palate and abnormal loose skin; the empty definition and nonspecific ancestry provide no basis for additional axes.
Bacterial infection umbrella with variable anatomical sites; no single organ is consistently affected across the group.
Glycosylation disorder with defining brain disease and hepatic abnormalities. Skeletal dysplasia occurs in 4/4; cardiac findings (30-79%) omitted at cap.
Primary carcinoma of the endometrium, a reproductive organ outside the thirteen axes; no qualifying extrauterine involvement is specified.
MYC-activated subtype of atypical teratoid rhabdoid tumor arising in the central nervous system.
Hair, skin and neurodevelopmental disease; brachydactyly/joint hypermobility and dental malocclusion each reported in 1/1 patient. Population frequencies remain uncertain.
Neoplasm originates in the urinary bladder, included in the renal axis. Intestinal-like morphology does not imply gastrointestinal involvement.
Inherited leukodystrophy; optic atrophy occurs in 30-79%. Bladder and bowel symptoms reflect neural dysfunction without documented intrinsic urinary or intestinal injury.
Malignant tumor originates in the peripheral nerve sheath; melanin production does not imply a cutaneous origin.
Cerebral motor disorder affecting all four limbs; fixed muscle-tendon contractures and skeletal deformity develop in more than 30% over the typical severe course.
